purpose: Run zizmor's credential-backed online audits (known-vulnerable-actions, impostor-commit, ref-confusion, ref-version-mismatch) against this repository's real workflows, since existing retained evidence is offline regular-persona analysis only (ci-security README lines 48-52), and confirm the online audits genuinely execute (network activity with the provided token) rather than silently no-op. FIX ROUND CORRECTION (2026-09-23): the original receipt omitted the first (tag-pinned) positive-control run, misattributed the ref-version-mismatch finding from the second run to the tj-actions pin instead of the actions/checkout pin, and drew a supports_incumbent conclusion the two runs together do not establish; this revision discloses both runs, retains both fixtures, and corrects the direction. No check was re-run to obtain a different outcome; the disclosed runs are the ones originally executed.
preregistered: If `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) zizmor --persona=auditor .github/workflows` (no --offline, no --no-online-audits) produces a nonempty HTTP cache directory and/or at least one online-only-audit finding on a constructed positive-control fixture, that demonstrates online audits genuinely execute with the supplied credential, settling the connectivity/credential half of gap 5. The findings on the real repository workflows themselves are recorded as-is, whatever they are (zero known-vulnerable-actions findings would be a real negative result supporting current action pinning hygiene, not a failure of this check). Two positive-control fixture variants were preregistered together: a tag-pinned form (tj-actions/changed-files@v45.0.7, the exact tag covered by GHSA-mrrh-fwg8-r2c3) and a SHA-pinned form (the same tag's resolved commit SHA). If known-vulnerable-actions fires on either form, that settles the 'online audits detect a real known-compromised action' half of gap 5 directly. If it fires on neither, that is recorded as a real negative result on this audit for this specific advisory, not retried against a different action/advisory to fish for a hit.

result: Ran zizmor's --persona=auditor scan with a real GH_TOKEN and no --offline/--no-online-audits flag against every published workflow in .github/workflows. 29 findings total, all from persona-gated static audits (anonymous-definition, concurrency-limits, secrets-outside-env) already reachable without a token; zero findings from the three online-credential-only audit idents (known-vulnerable-actions, impostor-commit, ref-confusion) named in the gap's next_check. Two positive-control fixtures pinning tj-actions/changed-files to v45.0.7 (covered by the real March-2025 GHSA-mrrh-fwg8-r2c3 compromise) were built and run the same way, one tag-pinned and one SHA-pinned to the exact compromised-era commit. Neither fixture produced a known-vulnerable-actions, impostor-commit or ref-confusion finding for the tj-actions/changed-files step in either pinning form. The tag-pinned fixture instead produced unpinned-uses on both steps (an offline audit, not evidence online audits ran). The SHA-pinned fixture produced ref-version-mismatch, which is an online-only audit and does prove online audits execute with this credential -- but it fired on the actions/checkout step (whose SHA resolves to tag v3.5.2, not the v4 the workflow's trailing comment claims), not on the tj-actions/changed-files step that is the actual subject of the compromise being tested for. The HTTP cache directory was independently populated with 20 real cache entries during the real-workflow run, corroborating that outbound network calls occur. So: online audits are confirmed to genuinely execute with this credential (via the HTTP cache and via ref-version-mismatch firing on an unrelated, correctly-mismatched pin), but the specific claim under test -- that zizmor's online known-vulnerable-actions audit would catch a workflow pinning to the exact commit behind a known, real, disclosed action compromise -- was tested twice (tag-pinned and SHA-pinned) and it did not fire either time.

verdict_impact.explanation: Online audits are proven to genuinely execute against this repository with the existing gh token (HTTP cache activity plus a correctly-triggered ref-version-mismatch finding on an unrelated pin). That part supports the incumbent's 'online credential-backed checks now run' claim. But the specific online-credential-only audit named in the gap text as the target capability -- known-vulnerable-actions -- was tested against a known, real, disclosed action compromise (GHSA-mrrh-fwg8-r2c3) in both a tag-pinned and a SHA-pinned form, and did not fire in either case. That is evidence against, not for, the 'online advisories' half of gap 5's coverage claim. Recorded as inconclusive rather than refutes_incumbent because it is possible zizmor's known-vulnerable-actions matcher requires a different signal (e.g. an advisory keyed to a different SHA range, or a GitHub Advisory Database entry it queries live rather than a static list) that this fixture did not trigger for a reason unrelated to coverage -- that alternative explanation was not ruled out.

limitations: known-vulnerable-actions specifically did not fire on either the tag-pinned or the SHA-pinned positive-control fixture (tj-actions/changed-files at v45.0.7 / its exact compromised-era commit SHA). This was tested twice, with two different pin forms, and neither triggered it; that is stronger evidence of a real coverage gap than a single run would be, though it still does not prove the audit never covers this incident (e.g. it might require a live GitHub Advisory Database lookup keyed in a way this fixture's exact SHA does not match, which was not independently verified).

This is one dated run against one repository's workflows on one day; it does not establish ongoing/scheduled online-audit coverage (that is a separate CI-configuration question, out of scope here -- validate.yml's zizmor step, per test_workflow_security.py etc., currently runs offline regular-persona only, not online auditor-persona, in CI).

The ref-version-mismatch finding that proves online audits execute is incidental: it flagged an unrelated tag/SHA mismatch on the actions/checkout step (SHA resolves to v3.5.2 while the trailing comment says v4), not the tj-actions/changed-files compromise the fixture was built to test. It demonstrates online execution, not known-vulnerable-actions coverage.

The real-workflow scan (.github/workflows) was run twice (zizmor-online-auditor.json and its -v2 rerun); both runs produced byte-identical output (sha256 480f1df2...), so the rerun changes no conclusion, but only the -v2 artifact was originally retained/disclosed.
